items.summary: The JSP Nepal parliamentary party leader was appointed under Article 168(3) of the constitution after no coalition secured a claim to form the provincial government.

items.title: Nepse loses ground as trading slows and investors favour select stocks
items.summary: Banking and selected hydropower stocks show relative strength, but falling daily turnover and weak economic growth prospects limit the market’s recovery.

items.title: Nepali cinema can’t stop playing ‘blame the buhari’ game
items.summary: A pattern in recent films casts women’s ambitions as threats to family harmony, reinforcing familiar stereotypes.

items.title: No Indian minister to attend India-Nepal business roundtable during Shah’s state visit
items.summary: The absence of Indian ministerial representation at the November 22 roundtable comes as Prime Minister Balendra Shah seeks greater investment from Nepal’s southern neighbour during his state visit.

items.title: Nepal has failed disaster survivors before. Can Bhotekoshi be different?
items.summary: Past relocation schemes have left families in unsafe settlements or driven them home. A 55-year-old settlement in Kanchanpur offers lessons as the government plans to relocate Bhotekoshi flood survivors.

items.title: Why a viral TikTok about ‘baddies’ has struck such a nerve in Nepal
items.summary: When a TikToker declared Nepal’s young women an ‘epidemic’, they answered with stethoscopes, spreadsheets and sarcasm.

items.title: NPL final tickets sell out in seconds. Was it craze or embezzlement, fans question
items.summary: CAN and eSewa officials say the matter resulted from a large number of users accessing the app. They rule out black marketing.

items.title: Lumbini and Sudurpaschim’s final clash will find the NPL’s ultimate team
items.summary: Lumbini Lions and Sudurpaschim Royals, the NPL’s most successful teams, meet for the third consecutive final, with Lumbini seeking to defend their title and Sudurpaschim aiming to end their run of heartbreak.

items.title: Victims of sexual violence during Maoist insurgency still await justice
items.summary: Saturday marks two decades since the Comprehensive Peace Accord was signed, but survivors of conflict-related sexual violence have yet to receive any form of justice even after filing complaints.

items.title: RSP joins local polls race as old parties move to guard their base
items.summary: The party has opened its Candidate Club for aspiring candidates, while the Congress, the UML and the Nepali Communist Party seek to retain and expand their local electoral base.

items.title: Two ex-ministers among ten arrested in Rs1.69 billion Malaysia fee racket
items.summary: Police say Nepali workers were charged an unauthorised 100-ringgit each, with 90 percent of the proceeds transferred to Malaysia through Nepal Rastra Bank.

items.title: Nepal's investment reforms yet to restore business confidence
items.summary: Business leaders say policy uncertainty, bureaucratic hurdles, local taxes and poor infrastructure continue to deter investment despite government pledges to improve the business climate.

items.title: India calls Shah’s visit ‘very important’, promises full state honours
items.summary: Kathmandu and New Delhi are still negotiating the key agenda items, possible deliverables and outcomes of the visit, as well as the contents of the joint communiqué and joint vision paper to be issued at its conclusion.

items.title: Nepali rock gets its moment on the world stage
items.summary: At 26, Bhojpur-born singer Pratik Himal Rai represented Nepal at Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok, and won over audiences even as he finished ninth.
